ShortDescription.Value: Co-op multiplayer for Cities: Skylines II: host a city and build it together with your friends over Steam. Works with your mods: dedicated support for Traffic, Move It, Anarchy and 9 more.

Publish.LongDescription:
# Skyline Together
Co-op multiplayer for Cities: Skylines II. One player hosts their city, friends join and get a copy of it, and from then on everything anyone builds is shared live. The host's game runs the simulation; the other players' games show the host's city and send their actions to the host, which checks and applies them for everyone.
**Before you play:** back up your saves. All players need the same version of Skyline Together, the same game version and the same gameplay mods (see below).
## What is shared
- Roads, buildings, zoning, districts, transport lines, terrain and water - Budget, taxes, loans, policies, milestones and unlocks - Traffic, citizens, vehicles and the numbers in the info panels - Game speed (the host's speed is everyone's; builders can change it for all) - Other players' cursors with name tags, their building previews in their colour, and chat
## Works with your mods
- **Dedicated support for 12 mods:** Traffic, Move It, Anarchy, Better Bulldozer, Tree Controller, Water Features, Plop the Growables, 529 Tiles, Historical Start, Zoning Toolkit, Line Tool and Find It. Their saved data, their tools and the settings that affect the simulation are shared by all players. - **Any other code mod** is analysed automatically when a session starts: its saved data replicates, its simulation runs on the host and its tools are captured like player edits. - **Mod settings from the host:** settings that change the simulation use the host's values for everyone; your own values come back when you leave. - **A clear join screen:** when mods differ, it lists exactly what to enable, disable or update. Mods that only change your own screen (translations, tooltips, icon libraries, overlays) may differ. - **Join anyway:** the host can let players join with harmless differences. Mods that store data in the city are always required, because the game cannot load the city without them. - **For mod authors:** an integration API to declare what your mod does and to send data to your mod on other PCs (see MOD-INTEGRATION.md on GitHub).
## How to play
**Host:** load a city, click the Skyline Together button in the top-left corner and press **Host this city**. Send your friends your Steam ID (copy icon at the top of the panel) or use **Invite friends**.
**Join:** on the title screen click **Multiplayer**, then **Join a friend**. Paste the host's Steam ID and the password if there is one, and press **Join**, or accept the host's Steam invite. Your game downloads and loads the host's city; the host's game pauses until you are in. Press **Enter** to chat.
No port forwarding is needed for Steam joins. Direct IP connections are optional and need a forwarded UDP port.
## Requirements and compatibility
- Steam version of the game on Windows, with Steam running. - Every player needs the **same version of Skyline Together** (the panel shows a build id: it must be the same on every PC), the **same game version** and, by default, the **same code mods** in the same versions. - Use the same asset subscriptions on every PC. Objects whose asset a player lacks are left out on that player's game. - **Not compatible with other multiplayer mods.** Disable them. - **Install it only once.** Do not keep a copy in the local Mods folder (from the GitHub installer) while you are subscribed here: the game then loads only one of them. Skyline Together warns at start when it finds two copies. - A game update can switch features off until the mod is updated; the startup self-test (shown in the Skyline Together panel) shows which.
## Known limitations
- Repairs of differences happen in the background and can take a moment. - The host's upload speed limits large sessions.
## Bugs, documentation and source code
Everything is on GitHub: https://github.com/ljkx/SkylineTogether The user guide, the FAQ and troubleshooting are in the docs folder there. To report a bug, every player clicks **Write diagnostics** in the panel; then attach the newest SkylineTogether-diagnostics file and SkylineTogether.log from the Logs folder in %USERPROFILE%\AppData\LocalLow\Colossal Order\Cities Skylines II of every player to a GitHub issue. The files contain player names and Steam IDs. Never attach crash dumps (.dmp) to a public issue: they can contain passwords.

Publish.ChangeLog:
First release on Paradox Mods.
- Host a loaded city; join by Steam ID, Steam invite or direct IP; optional password; 2 to 16 players - The host's city is saved, streamed to the joining player and loaded; the host pauses while someone joins - Host-authoritative sync of structures, economy, terrain, water, traffic, citizens and vehicles; every player builds with the normal tools - Roles, kick and ban, cursors with name tags, building previews, chat, shared game speed - Automatic integrity checks and repair, resync and reconnect - Works with your mods: dedicated support for 12 popular mods, automatic analysis of other code mods, a readable list of what to change - Solo test: record a session and verify it on one PC
Full changelog: https://github.com/ljkx/SkylineTogether/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
